requirements.name: relational-storage
requirements.text:
It stores everything in a relational database through the shipped persistence library, and every command either completes in full or changes nothing.

All database access goes through the shipped persistence library and the relational layer generated from `DATABASE.md`. Application code never opens a database driver directly.

requirements.name: command-interface
requirements.text:
The product is an executable named `ledger` at the application root.

The contract below is the same for every language and database: the same commands, the same output, and the same exit codes.

requirements.name: schema-lifecycle
requirements.text:
`ledger init` | Drops all three tables if present and creates them empty. Nothing written.

`ledger count` | `table,rows`, then `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions` rows in that order.

requirements.name: bulk-load
requirements.text: `ledger load <table> <csv>` | Loads `accounts`, `categories`, or `transactions` from a file whose header matches the table's columns in the order above. Writes `table,loaded` and `<table>,<rows>`.

requirements.name: account-management
requirements.text:
`ledger account add <code> <name>` | The new account row.

`ledger account get <code>` | The account row.

`ledger account rename <code> <name>` | The updated account row.

`ledger account delete <code>` | `deleted` and the code. Refused while the account has transactions.

requirements.name: transaction-management
requirements.text:
`ledger txn post <account> <category> <amount> <date> [<memo>]` | The new transaction row.

`ledger txn get <id>` | The transaction row.

`ledger txn amend <id> <amount>` | The updated transaction row. Only the amount changes.

`ledger txn delete <id>` | `deleted` and the id.

requirements.name: paired-transfers
requirements.text: `ledger transfer <from> <to> <amount> <date>` | Two transaction rows in category `TRANSFER`: `-amount` on `<from>` with memo `transfer to <to>`, then `+amount` on `<to>` with memo `transfer from <from>`. The amount is positive and the accounts differ.

requirements.name: balance-reports
requirements.text: `ledger report balances` | `account,name,transactions,balance` per account ordered by code, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<sum>`.

requirements.name: aggregate-reports
requirements.text:
`ledger report categories` | `category,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per category ordered by code, including categories with no transactions, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`.

`ledger report monthly` | `month,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per `YYYY-MM` that has transactions, ascending, then `TOTAL,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`.

requirements.name: non-negative-balances
requirements.text: No command leaves an account balance below zero. An account's balance is the sum of its transaction amounts. Posting, amending, deleting, transferring, and loading are all subject to this rule, checked before the command writes anything.

requirements.name: conformance-suite
requirements.text: The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs its own automated test suite from the application root and exits zero only when every test passes. The suite covers each command, each exit code, and each rule above against a real temporary database.

requirements.name: ledger-command
requirements.text: The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.

requirements.name: database-configuration
requirements.text: Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory.
